label: Linear Functions
overview: A linear function has the form f(x) = mx + b and produces a constant rate of change. SAT questions ask you to interpret slope as a rate of change (e.g., dollars per hour), interpret the y-intercept as a starting value, evaluate the function at a given input, or determine the equation from a table or graph.

workedExamples.problem: A linear function f satisfies f(2) = 11 and f(5) = 20. Write the equation of f(x).

steps.title: Calculate the slope
steps.content: Use the two given points (2, 11) and (5, 20).

steps.title: Find the y-intercept
steps.content: Use f(x) = 3x + b and plug in one known point, say (2, 11).

commonMistakes.mistake: Confusing slope and y-intercept when interpreting a real-world function
commonMistakes.fix: Slope is the per-unit rate (what changes per extra x). The y-intercept is the flat starting value when x = 0.

commonMistakes.mistake: Computing slope as (x₂−x₁)/(y₂−y₁) instead of rise over run
commonMistakes.fix: Slope = Δy/Δx (change in output divided by change in input). y always goes on top.

quickTip: In context questions, the slope always carries units: 'dollars per hour,' 'meters per second.' The y-intercept is usually a starting amount or fixed value.
